body:
**Stan Weinstein Stage Analysis (*Secrets for Profiting in Bull and Bear Markets*, 1988)**
- Uses weekly charts and the 30-week moving average (~150-day). Stage 1 basing (flat 30-week MA, price whipsawing around it); Stage 2 advancing (price breaks out above resistance and the 30-week MA turns up, on volume at least ~2x average on the breakout week); Stage 3 topping (MA flattens, price chops around it); Stage 4 declining (price below a falling 30-week MA). Buy only Stage 2 breakouts (or the first pullback to the breakout level); never hold in Stage 4. Uses Mansfield relative strength (stock vs. index, zero line) — RS should be positive/rising. Market and sector also must be in Stage 2 ("forest to trees"). Stop: below the prior base/support, then trail under the 30-week MA. — [MarketInOut Stage 2 screen (India)](https://www.marketinout.com/stock-screener/stage-2-uptrend/india) [F] for framework; detailed rules [K] from book.

**Nicolas Darvas box (*How I Made $2,000,000 in the Stock Market*, 1960)**
- Combined "techno-fundamental": stocks in growing industries with rising earnings, making new highs on unusual volume. A "box" forms when price makes a high not exceeded for ~3 days (top) and a low not broken for ~3 days (bottom). Buy-stop just above the box top; stop-loss just below the box bottom (or the new box's bottom as price stacks new boxes higher). — [Wikipedia: Nicolas Darvas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicolas_Darvas) [K]

**Jesse Livermore pivotal points (*How to Trade in Stocks*, 1940; *Reminiscences of a Stock Operator*)**
- Buy when price breaks through a "pivotal point" (a key prior high/resistance, or a round number) with confirming volume; "probe" with a small position, add only if the first is profitable (pyramid up, never average down); if the stock doesn't act right quickly after crossing the pivot, exit. Also: follow the leaders of leading groups ("tandem trading"). — [Wikipedia: Jesse Livermore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_Livermore) [K]

**Dan Zanger**
- Chart-pattern breakout trader (cup-with-handle, flags, pennants, ascending triangles) in high-volume leaders; requires breakout volume well above average; tight stops near the breakout point and fast exits if the breakout fails. Reportedly turned ~$10,775 into $18M+ in 1998-99 (widely cited; I found no independently audited record this session). [K] — gap: not verified this session.

body:
**Bull case**
- FY27 revenue of about ₹1,450 cr (+24% guidance) at 21–22% OPM gives PAT of about ₹205–215 cr.
- FY28 assumes an ag upcycle on top of construction: revenue of about ₹1,750 cr at 22% gives PAT of about ₹260 cr, or EPS of about ₹58.
- A re-rating to 20x gives about ₹1,150, roughly 1.6x in about two years, with dividends on top (FY26 payout was over 100%).
- Multibagger path: an ag-cycle recovery while construction holds would bring a return to FY23's 32% ROCE and EPS above ₹70.

**Risks**
- It is a deep cyclical. The FY24–25 drawdown cut PAT by 57%.
- **Inventory days are about 409 and the CCC is 326.** The warehousing model is working-capital heavy.
- Farm demand is still in a slump.
- Freight costs are high.
- A US tariff reset, or a rupee rebound toward ₹88.
- Customer concentration among large off-highway OEMs.

**Kill criteria**
- OPM below 18% for two consecutive quarters.
- Inventory days above 450 together with CFO below 60% of PAT.
- The promoter selling below 60%, or any pledge appearing.
- FY27 revenue growth below 15%, which would mean the guidance was missed badly.

`insight:cloning-indian-superstars` | confidence: **single-source** | tags: india, process, cloning, base-rate, smallcap

Indian shareholding disclosures only show holders with >=1% of a company, filed quarterly (typically within ~3 weeks of quarter-end), so a follower sees entries 1-4 months late, never sees sub-1% holdings, and usually learns of exits only after the next filing. Media 'X buys Y' stories routinely move small caps 5-20% on the news (observed pattern; magnitude unverified), so the follower's entry price is worse than the investor's. Superstar books are large and diversified (Mukul Agrawal ~72 stocks, Kacholia ~45-49, Dolly Khanna ~12-20 frequently churned), so any single disclosed stock may be a 0.5% experiment for them but a 20% bet for you. Survivorship: lists of 'superstar multibaggers' omit the many holdings that fell 50%+ in 2018-19 and 2025. Pabrai's cloning works better because he clones concentrated, long-held positions of investors with published reasoning, and still applies his own checklist. Useful use: treat disclosed stakes as a pre-screened idea list; check the investor's average cost (bulk-deal or filing prices), the stock's governance and valuation now, and size by your conviction, not theirs.

| key | value |
|---|---|
| lesson | use as idea source, not signal; check lag, size and price paid |

Links: person:ashish-kacholia (about); person:dolly-khanna (about); person:mukul-agrawal (about); person:mohnish-pabrai (about); insight:behavior-gap (about)

body:
**Scoring each resolved promise:**
- `delivered` (≥ 95% of target, on time) = +1; `partially_delivered` (≥ 70% or ≤ 1 quarter late) = +0.5; `missed` = −1; `moved_goalpost` (deadline pushed or metric redefined *without* acknowledging a miss) = −1.5; `withdrawn` with candid explanation = −0.5. "Silent drop" = −1.5.
- Weight by specificity (0–3) and materiality (share of revenue/EBIT affected).
- Beat-and-raise behaviour: consistent under-promising (delivery_ratio around 1.1–1.3) is *good*.

**Management Credibility Score (MCS)**, rolling 12 quarters:
`MCS = Σ(w_i · score_i) / Σ w_i`, where `w_i = specificity_i × materiality_i × recency_decay` (half-life about 8 quarters).
Report alongside it: hit rate, average delivery ratio, average delay in quarters, count of moved goalposts, and **candour index** (share of misses that management acknowledged unprompted in the next call).
Also track a **guidance-to-tone gap**: optimistic language (LM positive minus negative, or LLM-rated) against MCS. India evidence says the market pays for tone, so high tone with low MCS is the short-side or avoid signal, and low-key tone with high MCS is the under-recognised compounder.

**Change detectors** to run every quarter, from the endpoints above:
- Promoter pledge up, SAST promoter sale, or a PIT sell cluster near results.
- Auditor resignation or qualification; CFO change (Lazy Prices found CEO/CFO text changes predictive).
- Credit rating watch-negative or "issuer not cooperating".
- Bulk deals by known funds versus operators.
- Spike in related-party-transaction approvals in AGM notices.
- Concall topic diff (new risk words, dropped KPIs, sudden length/complexity increase).

- **id:** `thesis:paper-call:ULTRACEMCO:q3fy27-op-4500cr-plus`
- **Method:** management-tone-vs-delivery · **P(ours)** 0.45 · **P(base)** 0.50 · resolve by 2027-02-28
- **Evidence:** Q2 FY27 call (19-Oct-2026): volume +13.8% YoY, utilisation 71%, fuel and raw-material costs up (West Asia), other fixed cost/t −6%; Chairman's-office commentary: trade prices rose ₹7–10/bag in late September, 'Prices… have risen substantially in the month of October and continue to stay high. My sense is that there is more price improvement that will happen… in the next couple of months', 'full benefit… in the Q3 earnings'; South 'transforming. Mark my words.' Screener (₹ cr): OP Q3 FY26 3,911 (OPM 17.9%), Q4 FY26 5,599, Q1 FY27 5,015, Q2 FY27 3,719 (16.0%); sales Q2 FY27 23,295 (+19%).
- **Why our number differs from base:** ₹4,500 cr needs roughly sales ~₹24.5k cr at ~18.4% OPM, i.e. the October price hikes must largely stick through the post-Diwali lull while fuel stays expensive. Management is unusually emphatic about prices; Indian cement hikes announced in October are often partly rolled back in November–December. We lean slightly below base.
- **Base-rate reasoning:** Naive: Q3 operating profit grows ~15% YoY in line with volume growth plus modest pricing, landing near ₹4,500 cr — a coin-flip-ish 50%.
- **Resolution rule:** YES if UltraTech's consolidated Operating Profit (screener.in quarterly table; equivalently EBITDA excluding other income from the results) for the quarter ended 31-Dec-2026 is ≥₹4,500 cr.
- **Resolution source:** UltraTech Cement Q3 FY27 results (NSE) / screener.in consolidated quarterly table

body:
- **US gate in `score.py`.** A promise is US if its id starts `promise:US-`, or its `symbol` starts `US-`, or `market` is `us`. US
  promises use only the US vocabulary below and **never fall through** to the India/screener measures (INR cr, OPM, debtor days).
  If no US measure matches, the result is *not-auto-scorable* ("US company: no recognised US measure").
  | Measure | Phrases it catches (metric text first) | Scored from |
  |---|---|---|
  | `organic_growth_pct` | "organic" | `--csv` only (company-reported) |
  | `net_sales_growth_pct` | "net sales", "sales/revenue growth", "top line" | `--csv` (SEC XBRL or release) |
  | `segment_sales_growth_pct`, `segment_margin_pct` | the metric names a segment, region, product line or country (Americas, International, Europe, APMEA, Rest of World, North America, boiler, water treatment/heater, automation, Harris, China, India, Leonard) | `--csv` only |
  | `adj_op_margin_pct` / `gaap_op_margin_pct` | "adjusted operating", "operating (income) margin" (GAAP only when the text says "GAAP") | `--csv` only |
  | `adj_ebitda_margin_pct` | "EBITDA" | `--csv` only |
  | `adj_eps_usd` / `gaap_eps_usd` | "EPS", "per share" ("adjusted" or "continuing" -> adjusted) | `--csv` only |
  | `fcf_conversion_pct`, `cash_return_pct_fcf`, `fcf_usd_mn` | "cash conversion", "FCF / net income"; "return ... of free cash flow"; "free cash flow" | `--csv` only |
  | `capex_usd_mn`, `buyback_usd_mn`, `cost_savings_usd_mn`, `price_realisation_usd_mn` | "capex"; "repurchase/buyback"; "savings", "operating expenses"; "price/cost", "price actions" | `--csv` only |
  - Multi-year targets (CAGR, a year 2030+, "across the cycle") and segment/acquired-business **dollar** amounts ("Leonard Valve ~$70 mn") return *not-auto-scorable* (judgment).
  - Margins and ratios use the 0.3 / 1.5 pp thresholds and growth uses the growth thresholds (the sets join `PP_MEASURES` / `GROWTH_MEASURES`); amounts use the 95% / 80% ratio rule.
- **`parse_target(text, us=False)`:** with `us=True` (passed automatically for US promises) it also parses per-share ranges ("$3.42 to $3.52" -> 3.42-3.52 USD/share; "$0.96") and the US growth words "low single digit" 1-3%, "mid single digit" 4-6%, "low teens" 11-13%, "mid teens" 14-16%. India/IT parsing is unchanged.
  - **Known limit:** bp-expansion targets ("+50 to +110 bp") are still read by the bank bps rule as 0.50-1.10 *%* levels. Score these by hand on the expansion (clarification B), or give `target_low/high` explicitly.
- **Scoring US ledgers:** the four 2026-11-22 ledgers were built by hand (`research_notes/Promise tracker pilot/scripts_us_industrials/promises_US-*.py`), not through `fetch.py` (which reads NSE). For a pipeline run on a US company, pass the Motley Fool HTML converted to text, or the 8-K Ex 99.1 press release, as `--local FILE@YYYY-MM-DD` (pdf_to_text is skipped for .txt only if you pre-place the .txt in the cache; simplest is to print the page to PDF). Supply company figures in the `--csv` (field = measure name).
- **Regression check:** all 426 promises in the existing `memdb/seeds/*promises*.json` (India + IT, excluding the new US seed) give the same `infer_measure` and `parse_target` result as v1.2 (0 changed).
- **Scoreboard (`tools/scoreboard/resolve.py`):** `sec_fact` gained `operating_income` (OperatingIncomeLoss), `capex` (PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment, else PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets) and the ratio `op_margin_pct` = 100 x operating income / revenue (both first-reported, same period rules). One new unit test.
- **Data access notes (US):** fool.com quote pages (`/quote/nyse/<t>/`) list the transcript URLs. Several calls had no Fool page (WTS Q3-25, SSD Q2-26, LECO Q2-25 and Q2-26); guessed slugs 404. Use the 8-K Item 2.02 Exhibit 99.1 instead: `python3 tools/sec_fetch.py filings T --form 8-K --items 2.02`, then `doc T ACCESSION --file <ex99 name> --text` (the `--file` flag is needed; without it the 8-K cover document is downloaded). Lincoln Electric's releases carry almost no outlook; Watts, A. O. Smith and Simpson put the outlook in the release.
